summary: Covers installing collections with `ansible-galaxy collection install`: the default Galaxy server and install path (`~/.ansible/collections`), upgrading with `--upgrade`, and installing from a tarball, a source directory, or a namespace directory. Notes that `-p` gets `ansible_collections` appended automatically unless already under such a folder.
questions: How do I install a collection from Ansible Galaxy?

answer_card.title: Install a collection with ansible-galaxy
answer_card.answer_md:
By default `ansible-galaxy collection install` uses https://galaxy.ansible.com and installs into `~/.ansible/collections/ansible_collections`; no extra configuration is needed.

```bash
ansible-galaxy collection install my_namespace.my_collection
# upgrade to latest
ansible-galaxy collection install my_namespace.my_collection --upgrade
# from a built tarball
ansible-galaxy collection install my_namespace-my_collection-1.0.0.tar.gz -p ./collections
# build+install from source (uses MANIFEST.json or galaxy.yml)
ansible-galaxy collection install /path/to/collection -p ./collections
# all collections in a namespace dir
ansible-galaxy collection install /path/to/ns -p ./collections
```

Note: `-p` automatically gets `ansible_collections` appended unless the parent directory is already named `ansible_collections`. For other Galaxy servers (e.g. Automation Hub) configure the ansible-galaxy client.
